title: How Cattle Plague, Tick Fever and a Kenyan Vaccine Eradicated Rinderpest and Launched One Health — Lancisi's Cattle Quarantine, Theobald Smith's 1893 Four-Pen Tick Proof, Loeffler's 125,000× Filterable Virus Dilution, Mariner's ThermoVax Pastoralist Herd Immunity (85.5% > 80% R₀=5) & Serengeti Cascade

teenKit.tldr: Most people think only smallpox was ever wiped out by humans, but rinderpest—a brutal cattle plague with up to 95% mortality—was successfully eradicated globally in 2011.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Beating rinderpest didn't just save livestock and prevent mass human famines; it proved that veterinary and human medicine are permanently linked through the powerful concept of 'One Health.'
keyTakeaways: Rinderpest, meaning 'cattle plague' in German, was a devastating viral biological wrecking ball that haunted agriculture for thousands of years.
Only two infectious diseases have ever been completely eradicated from planet Earth by human action: smallpox and rinderpest.
Advanced scientific detective work—from historical quarantines and tick-proof pens to modern genetic sequencing and thermo-stable vaccines—made the total extinction of the virus possible.

vocab.meaning: A highly contagious and lethal viral disease affecting cattle and wild ungulates, characterized by severe tissue destruction and near-100% mortality.
The complete and permanent global elimination of a natural infectious agent so that zero cases exist anywhere in the world.
The collaborative approach recognizing that human health, animal health, and the environment are deeply interconnected.
A hoofed mammal, which includes domesticated livestock like cattle and wild animals like antelopes and giraffes.

quiz.question: How many infectious diseases have humans officially and completely eradicated from nature?
options: Five (Smallpox, Polio, Rinderpest, Measles, and Malaria)
quiz.explanation: While smallpox is the most famous, rinderpest was officially certified as globally eradicated in 2011, making it the second.

quiz.question: What does the German word 'Rinderpest' literally translate to in English?
quiz.explanation: Rinderpest translates directly to 'cattle plague,' capturing its terrifying and destructive historical impact.

quiz.question: Why is the defeat of rinderpest considered a monumental victory for 'One Health'?
options: It only affected wild animals in remote jungles.
It proved that protecting animal populations and agriculture directly safeguards human survival and food security.
It relied entirely on human vaccines rather than animal treatments.
It happened purely by accident without scientific intervention.
quiz.explanation: One Health bridges animal and human medicine, showing that wiping out a devastating livestock plague protects human societies from starvation and economic collapse.
